The Margin · a reading journal

Notes written in the gutter, the way a scribe would.

Every page has a wide margin. That is where the real reading happens — the marginalia, the glosses, the small arguments you have with the author.

The old scribes did not read the way we do. They did not scan a page for information and move on. They sat with a text the way you sit with a person, and they wrote back. The margin was not empty space to them. It was the room where the conversation happened.

When we read on screens, the margin disappears. The text fills the whole window edge to edge, and there is nowhere to write back. Reading becomes something that happens to you instead of something you do. The gloss is where reading becomes an act.

This journal keeps a wide margin on purpose. Not for decoration. The margin is the point. It is the space where you argue with the author, where you connect one book to another, where you write the thing you will only understand later.

gloss, n. — an explanation written in the margin; the reader talking back to the text.
The word marginal used to mean “written in the margin,” not “unimportant.”
Connect this to the notebooks you keep. The best notes are the ones in the edge.
Set in a face like the one the composer chose for parchment. Composed from DNA, not picked from a library.
